The GitHub satellite is alexar76/domain-operator-kit. # Domain Operator Kit Cloud PlatformsNetworking & InfrastructurePayments & Billing by alexar76 OverviewSchemaSourceRelated ServersDiscussionsAdmin JavaScript Local Which integrations are available for this server? Connects an owned domain to a Vercel project, using Vercel's current DNS recommendations, adding the apex domain to the pinned project, and preserving existing TXT verification values and unrelated records. Supports optional replacement of existing A records and reports whether Vercel configuration or DNS verification is still pending. How do I use Domain Operator Kit? 1. Click on "Deploy Server". 2. Wait a few minutes for the server to deploy. Once ready, it will show a "Started" state. 3. In the chat, type `@` followed by the MCP server name and your instructions, e.g., "`@Domain Operator Kit` quote and register example.com for a year, then attach it to my Vercel project" That's it! The server will respond to your query, and you can continue using it as needed. Here is a step-by-step guide with screenshots. > 🔄 Synced from a monorepo — but with a live history. `domain-kit` mirrors the canonical AI-Factory monorepo. History here is append-only (no force-push). Pull requests are welcome — merged PRs are imported back into the monorepo and re-synced here, so your contribution becomes canonical. 💬 Issues · Pull requests both welcome. An agent can build and deploy an application. This kit lets it take the next step: obtain a signed price for a domain, register it to its real owner, manage DNS and connect it to a Vercel project. Independent operators run their own seller nodes, use their own registrar accounts and set a fixed markup per registration or renewal. Agents use a shared capability contract and a budgeted MCP client. > Pre-live release. The local tests and Openprovider and Porkbun Sandbox pilots pass: registration, DNS, renewal, lost-response recovery and MCP reads. Production domain purchases, payment settlement and Vercel attachment remain unverified. The default demo buys nothing. Verification record → ## What the buyer gets One exact domain, registered for one year to the supplied registrant. The quote shows the supplier cost, fixed markup and final amount before payment. For example, a $10 supplier cost plus a $2 markup gives a 12 USDC order; these are illustrative amounts, not a registrar tariff. DNS management and domain information are included. Renewal is a separate purchase at a newly quoted price. Registrar autorenew is disabled. Availability is not a reservation, and registrant email verification may still require action by the owner. The built-in registrar scope is `.com`, `.net` and `.org`, ordinary ASCII names, one year. Premium names, IDNs, incoming transfers and expired-domain restoration are outside this release. Related MCP server: ClawDaddy MCP Server ## One product, three roles You are | What you use A domain operator or reseller | Your registrar account, receiving wallet, refund reserve and fixed markup; a seller node with durable orders An independent supplier | The HTTP supplier contract, implemented in your own language and infrastructure An agent or app developer | Signed `domains.*@v1` capabilities, the JavaScript client or the stdio MCP configuration `flowchart LR Agent["AI agent / MCP client"] -->|Discover| Hub["AIMarket Hub"] Hub -->|Public quotes only| Seller["Domain operator"] Agent -->|Private order + x402 payment| Seller Seller -->|Register and reconcile| Provider["Openprovider / Porkbun / HTTP supplier"] Agent -->|Owner-signed DNS| Seller Agent -->|Buyer-side connector| Vercel["Your Vercel project"]` The Hub handles discovery. Orders, registrant contacts, payment authorizations and DNS operations go directly to the seller. This implementation charges no Hub commission. The Vercel token stays with the buyer. ## Try it locally Use Node.js 22.13+; local verification used 22.22.1. From `domain-kit/` in the monorepo, or from the root of a satellite checkout: `npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run check npm test npm run demo` The demo runs a signed HTTP lifecycle: quote → simulated registration → DNS → renewal. No registrar account, wallet funding or external service is needed. Local HTTP tests require permission to listen on localhost. For the simplest external API test, use the Porkbun Sandbox quickstart: automatic disposable credentials, virtual credit and a resumable end-to-end pilot. The Porkbun adapter is sandbox-only until a production pilot passes. For the Openprovider Sandbox API integration test, follow the opt-in `npm run sandbox:pilot` instructions. The script retains its state and reuses the same orders on repeat runs. For a persistent demo server: `cp .env.example .env node --env-file=.env src/server.js` In another terminal: `DOMAIN_ALLOW_DEMO=1 node bin/domain-rails.mjs check http://127.0.0.1:9495` This checks the public quote protocol and signature; it does not certify the seller. The server persists encrypted documents and keys in `data/`. Do not discard that directory between deployments. ### A public node: demo until your keys are in `DOMAIN_MODE=auto` is for a node you publish before you sell. Without keys it is a public demo: availability is real (the registries' own RDAP for `.com`, `.net`, `.org`), quotes are signed and marked `demo` with illustrative prices, reads answer, and only `register` and `renew` are refused with `403 demo_mode`. When every live setting is in (production registrar keys or an HTTP supplier, `PAY_TO`, `CDP_KEY_FILE`, `DOMAIN_REFUND_KEY_FILE`, HTTPS `DOMAIN_PUBLIC_URL` and `DOMAIN_TERMS_URL`, `DOMAIN_UPSTREAM_COST_CONFIRMED=1`), the next start sells live. Until then `/healthz` lists the setting names still missing (`live_missing`), never their values. Porkbun stays sandbox-only. modelmarket.dev runs such a node as its domain showcase. ## Agent capabilities Capability | Purpose `domains.quote@v1` | Availability, exact registration price or private renewal quote `domains.register@v1` | Register the quoted name for one year `domains.renew@v1` | Renew an owned domain using a new quote `domains.order.status@v1` | Recover a pending order and retrieve its signed receipt `domains.info@v1` | Expiry, nameservers and required owner actions `domains.dns.get@v1` | DNS records and revision `domains.dns.set@v1` | Replace selected record sets while preserving other names and types `domains.transfer.code@v1` | Private transfer code, where supported; excluded from the MCP tool list Machine-readable contract · Authentication and payment protocol ### Connect a buyer `node bin/domain-rails.mjs init-owner /private/path/owner.pem` Adapt examples/mcp.json for a client that supports stdio MCP. Pin the seller's public key through a trusted catalog, configure the owner's signing key and contact file, then set a per-purchase and daily budget. Purchases default to disabled. `DOMAIN_REGISTRANT_FILE` injects the contact locally. Wallet and owner keys come from private files, never model arguments. Payment authorizations and budget reservations are persisted before sending. A retry reuses its original authorization; an unknown outcome keeps its budget reserved. Keep the original `client_order_id` and order body across retries. A pending response is a reason to check status, not to create a second purchase. The user or client policy must authorize purchases and acceptance of seller terms. ### Connect the domain to Vercel Configure `VERCEL_TOKEN_FILE`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` and optionally `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` in the buyer's environment. The MCP client exposes `vercelConnect`: `{"domain":"your-owned-domain.com"}` The connector uses Vercel's current DNS recommendations, adds the apex domain to the pinned project and preserves existing TXT verification values and unrelated records. Replacing other A records requires explicit `replace_existing:true`. Conflicting AAAA/CNAME records must first be removed through the DNS provider's console. `waiting_for_verification_or_dns` means propagation or verification is still pending. `configured` reflects the Vercel API, not an independent HTTPS reachability test. The seller itself requires a persistent Node process and disk; it is not a Vercel Function. ## Bring your supplier Openprovider and Porkbun Sandbox have built-in adapters. Other suppliers implement the common HTTP endpoints for quotes, contact preparation, submission, reconciliation and management. Operators retain their own accounts, pricing and payment destination. Supplier contract and runnable simulator → Supporting the contract makes integration possible; it does not make an untested supplier production-ready. Our pilot plan starts with Openprovider Sandbox and our own agent, then a controlled domain for our own Vercel project, before involving outside customers. ## Built for interrupted operations * Durable order identity. Changed input cannot silently reuse an existing order. A wallet signature binds payment to the order and owner key. * No blind mutation retries. Lost payment and registrar responses enter reconciliation using the original evidence. * Refunds for proven non-delivery. Refunds target the original payer. Ambiguous outcomes remain pending; refunds require a funded reserve and functioning infrastructure. * Private management. Owner requests and seller responses use Ed25519; document bodies use AES-256-GCM. Database row identifiers, including domain names, are not encrypted. * Explicit operational limits. One seller process per SQLite database. Openprovider renewal ambiguity may require documented operator evidence. Porkbun replays use a durable idempotency key only within a 23-hour window; older unknown outcomes require review. DNS revision checking is not an atomic lock against outside console edits. No automatic expiry notifications, renewal scheduler, owner-key recovery or general DNS deletion API is included. Operators must provide those support procedures before serving customers. See OPERATIONS.md. ## Repository status Canonical source is `domain-kit/` in the AIMarket monorepo. The GitHub satellite is alexar76/domain-operator-kit. From the monorepo root the same commands are `npm test --prefix domain-kit` (and `npm run check --prefix domain-kit`). A Node 22/24 CI workflow, Docker/Compose definitions and local branding assets are included. The workflow is prepared; this README does not claim it has run on GitHub. The local test badge links to a dated verification record. This package remains `private:true` to prevent accidental npm publication. No hosted demo or published package is implied by the quickstart. MIT licensed. Base payment reconciliation was adapted from the AIMarket eSIM operator kit; see NOTICE.md. ## Available Tools 7 tools dnsGetB Read-only Inspect Read owned DNS records and their revision before an update. dnsSetA Destructive Inspect Replace only named DNS record sets, preserving other names and types. Requires the current DNS revision. infoB Read-only Inspect Read an owned domain, expiry, nameservers and verification requirements. quoteA Read-only Inspect Quote a one-year domain registration or renewal. Renewal requires the owner signature. Availability is not a reservation. registerA Destructive Inspect Buy the exact domain in an unexpired quote, registered to the supplied registrant. Irreversible after registration. Separate x402 payment required. renewB Destructive Inspect Renew an owned domain for one year using a renewal quote. Separate payment; automatic registrar renewal is disabled. statusA Read-only Inspect Recover a private order after a lost response. Pending is not failure; never buy again to resolve a timeout. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- aicom · GitHub Topics · GitHub (https://github.itlym.cn/topics/aicom) 【turn914958search1】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; ### alexar76 / cite-desks ... First observed`v0.1.0`Oct 20, 2026 Does the description disclose side effects, auth requirements, rate limits, or destructive behavior? Annotations already declare readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true, and openWorldHint=true, so the safety profile is covered. The description adds useful non-annotated behavior: the renewal term is one year, payment is handled separately, and automatic registrar renewal is disabled. It does not cover failure modes or permission requirements, but it meaningfully extends the annotation-based profile. Agents need to know what a tool does to the world before calling it. Descriptions should go beyond structured annotations to explain consequences. Conciseness 4/5 Is the description appropriately sized, front-loaded, and free of redundancy? Two sentences, front-loaded with the core action and zero boilerplate. Every clause carries information, though the second sentence is slightly terse and could integrate parameter flow more usefully. Shorter descriptions cost fewer tokens and are easier for agents to parse. Every sentence should earn its place. Completeness 2/5 Given the tool's complexity, does the description cover enough for an agent to succeed on first attempt? For a destructive, open-world mutation with four required parameters all lacking schema descriptions and no output schema, the description is too thin. It omits what accept_terms/terms_version mean, whether client_order_id provides idempotency, and what happens on failure or partial payment, leaving important agent-relevant details unaddressed. Parameters 2/5 Does the description clarify parameter syntax, constraints, interactions, or defaults beyond what the schema provides? Schema description coverage is 0% and all four parameters are required, so the description must compensate. It only hints at 'quote_id' via 'using a renewal quote' and says nothing about accept_terms, terms_version, or client_order_id. This leaves most parameter meaning undocumented. Input schemas describe structure but not intent. Descriptions should explain non-obvious parameter relationships and valid value ranges. Purpose 4/5 Does the description clearly state what the tool does and how it differs from similar tools? States a specific verb and resource: 'Renew an owned domain for one year using a renewal quote.' This clearly separates it from the sibling 'register' (new domain) and implies dependence on 'quote'. However, it does not explicitly name an alternative tool or clarify scope against all siblings, so it falls just short of a 5. Agents choose between tools based on descriptions. A clear purpose with a specific verb and resource helps agents select the right tool. Usage Guidelines 3/5 Does the description explain when to use this tool, when not to, or what alternatives exist? The phrase 'using a renewal quote' implies the prerequisite flow of obtaining a quote first, and 'Separate payment; automatic registrar renewal is disabled' adds operational context.
